title: Effectiveness of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 (Arexvy®) vaccine against RSV-associated hospitalisations among older adults in Germany – a test-negative case-control study
summary:
Background
The RSV vaccine Arexvy® by GSK has been approved in Germany to protect older adults against serious respiratory illness caused by the Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). RSV can cause severe lower respiratory tract disease in people aged 60 and above and may require hospitalisation. This study is being conducted in German hospitals to assess the real-world benefit of the vaccine.

Research question
How effective is the RSV vaccine Arexvy® in preventing hospitalisation due to RSV lower respiratory tract infection in vaccinated individuals aged 60 and above, compared to unvaccinated individuals?

Methodology
The study observes patients admitted to hospital with respiratory symptoms. All participants provide a respiratory sample that is tested for RSV. The study then compares whether vaccinated individuals test positive less frequently than unvaccinated ones. Participation does not change the medical care patients receive. No new medications are administered. This is purely an observational study.
conditions: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)-associated acute respiratory illness (ARI) and lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) leading to hospitalisation in adults aged 60 years and above.

interventions.name:
Non-interventional, Real-world Effectiveness of Arexvy® (RSVPreF3 OA) Against RSV-Associated Lower Respiratory Tract Disease in Adults Aged ≥60 Years in Germany — REVEAL-DE

Cases: Test-positive case is hospitalized ARI/LRTD participant with at least one RSV-positive respiratory sample by RT-PCR,

Controls: Test-negative control is hospitalized ARI/LRTD participant with all respiratory samples RSV-negative by RT-PCR, collected within 10 days before or up to 72 hours after admission.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- The participant is hospitalized with LRTD/ARI for at least one day (the dates of 
admission and discharge differ by at least one day). 
- The participant is aged 60 to 74 years, with at least one chronic condition as a risk 
factor for severe RSV, or aged 75 years or older. 
- Informed consent is obtained from the participant or, when accepted by the Ethics 
Committee, from the participant’s legally acceptable representative(s) prior to 
enrollment. 
- A PCR test (used as standard of care in the hospital) result is obtained from the 
participant within 10 days prior to or up to 72 hours after hospital admission. 
Antigen testing will not be used for eligibility.
Exclusion criteria:
- The participant tests negative for RSV but positive for influenza and/or SARS-CoV
2 on a PCR test using the routine respiratory specimen.  
- The participant has been previously enrolled in the study (defined as signing the ICF) 
during any prior hospitalization episode. 
- The participant has been transferred to the study hospital from another inpatient 
healthcare facility.
